title: Oxidative hemolysis with bite cells: G6PD deficiency (glutathione reductase deficiency is analogous)
vignette: A 24-year-old man is evaluated for episodic anemia, jaundice, and dark urine. These episodes typically occur after the use of certain drugs or following infection. Additional history reveals that he has a brother who experiences similar episodes. Peripheral blood smear reveals red blood cells with the findings shown below: the smear shows cells with a semicircular portion removed from the periphery (bite cells). Deficiency of which of the following enzymes would most likely result in a condition similar to this patient's presentation?

clues.text: episodic anemia, jaundice, and dark urine
clues.note: Episodic anemia with jaundice and hemoglobinuria (dark urine) indicates episodic hemolysis.

clues.text: after the use of certain drugs or following infection
clues.note: Hemolysis triggered by OXIDANT stressors (drugs like sulfonamides/antimalarials, infection, fava beans) is characteristic of G6PD deficiency.
Affected males in the family fit X-LINKED RECESSIVE inheritance (G6PD deficiency).

clues.text: semicircular portion removed from the periphery (bite cells)
clues.note: BITE CELLS form when splenic macrophages remove Heinz bodies (oxidized, precipitated hemoglobin) - the hallmark of G6PD deficiency.

whatMatters: Oxidant-triggered hemolysis with BITE CELLS (and Heinz bodies) in an X-linked pattern = G6PD DEFICIENCY. G6PD generates NADPH to keep GLUTATHIONE reduced (antioxidant). GLUTATHIONE REDUCTASE deficiency causes an ANALOGOUS problem - inability to use NADPH to reduce glutathione. Answer B.
strategy: Recognize G6PD deficiency (oxidant-triggered hemolysis, bite cells/Heinz bodies, X-linked), then find the enzyme whose deficiency reproduces the SAME defect: failure of the glutathione antioxidant system. Glutathione reductase (regenerates reduced glutathione from NADPH) fits. Reject glycolytic/other enzymes: bisphosphoglycerate mutase (2,3-BPG, O2 offloading), hexokinase and pyruvate kinase (glycolytic ATP - hemolysis but no oxidant trigger/bite cells), and transketolase (nonoxidative PPP/ribose, no NADPH).

eliminations.label: Bisphosphoglycerate mutase - 2,3-BPG, O2 offloading
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: RBC enzyme making 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate, which promotes O2 offloading. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: its deficiency alters oxygen affinity, not oxidant defense; it wouldn't cause oxidant-triggered hemolysis with bite cells. ✅ Correct if: altered hemoglobin-oxygen affinity.

eliminations.label: Hexokinase - glycolytic ATP, no oxidant link
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the first glycolytic enzyme; deficiency reduces RBC ATP. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes chronic hemolysis from ATP lack, NOT oxidant-triggered hemolysis with bite cells/Heinz bodies. ✅ Correct if: nonspherocytic hemolysis from ATP depletion without oxidant trigger.

eliminations.label: Pyruvate kinase - glycolytic ATP deficiency
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a late glycolytic enzyme; deficiency lowers ATP and causes chronic hemolytic anemia. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: hemolysis is not oxidant-triggered and lacks bite cells/Heinz bodies; smear shows echinocytes/burr cells. ✅ Correct if: chronic hemolysis with rigid RBCs from ATP deficiency.

eliminations.label: Transketolase - nonoxidative PPP, no NADPH
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an enzyme of the NONoxidative pentose phosphate pathway (makes ribose; thiamine-dependent). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it does not generate NADPH, so its deficiency wouldn't impair the glutathione antioxidant system. ✅ Correct if: thiamine-related transketolase activity testing (Wernicke).

reasoning: Oxidant-triggered episodic hemolysis with bite cells and X-linked inheritance = G6PD deficiency
G6PD makes NADPH, which glutathione reductase uses to keep glutathione reduced (antioxidant defense)
Glutathione reductase deficiency likewise prevents regeneration of reduced glutathione
-> deficiency of glutathione reductase reproduces the same oxidant-hemolysis picture; answer B
mechanism: GLUCOSE-6-PHOSPHATE DEHYDROGENASE (G6PD) DEFICIENCY is an X-linked recessive disorder causing episodic HEMOLYTIC anemia and jaundice triggered by OXIDANT stress (sulfonamide/antimalarial drugs, infection, fava beans). G6PD is the rate-limiting enzyme of the pentose phosphate pathway and generates NADPH, the reducing agent needed to keep GLUTATHIONE in its reduced state; reduced glutathione detoxifies hydrogen peroxide and protects red cells from oxidative injury. Without adequate NADPH/reduced glutathione, oxidized hemoglobin precipitates as HEINZ BODIES, which splenic macrophages pluck out, forming BITE CELLS. GLUTATHIONE REDUCTASE catalyzes the NADPH-dependent regeneration of reduced glutathione; its deficiency produces an ANALOGOUS failure of the antioxidant system - the red cell cannot use NADPH to reduce glutathione - yielding a clinically SIMILAR oxidant-induced hemolysis. The distractors involve oxygen-affinity regulation (bisphosphoglycerate mutase), glycolytic ATP production (hexokinase, pyruvate kinase - chronic hemolysis without oxidant trigger/bite cells), or the nonoxidative PPP (transketolase, which makes ribose and does not generate NADPH).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Biochem/Heme > G6PD deficiency: X-linked; PPP -> NADPH -> reduced glutathione (antioxidant); oxidant-triggered hemolysis; Heinz bodies -> bite cells; glutathione reductase deficiency is analogous.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: G6PD -> NADPH -> reduced glutathione; glutathione reductase deficiency breaks the same antioxidant loop.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on G6PD, NADPH, reduced glutathione, Heinz bodies/bite cells, pentose phosphate pathway, or glutathione reductase? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Bisphosphoglycerate mutase = O2 offloading; hexokinase/pyruvate kinase = glycolytic ATP (no oxidant trigger/bite cells); transketolase = nonoxidative PPP (no NADPH).

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: Blood smear (stem): cells with a bite taken out of the rim = BITE CELLS (Heinz bodies removed by spleen) -> oxidative hemolysis (G6PD / glutathione antioxidant defect).

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: oxidant hemolysis + bite cells/Heinz bodies = G6PD deficiency; glutathione reductase deficiency mimics it (both fail to reduce glutathione).

keywords.back: Glutathione reductase (also fails to reduce glutathione)

firstAid.detail: Biochem: NADPH -> reduced glutathione; oxidant hemolysis, bite cells.
Heme > deficiency prevents glutathione reduction (same defect).
Biochem > pyruvate kinase/hexokinase (ATP), BPG mutase (O2), transketolase (ribose).

memoryHook: G6PD makes NADPH to keep glutathione's antioxidant shield charged; knock out glutathione reductase and the shield stays dead too - either way, oxidants bite chunks out of the red cells.
